title: FastDSAC: Unlocking the Potential of Maximum Entropy RL in High-Dimensional Humanoid Control
claim: Our method reaches much higher returns and learns faster than the strongest baseline on very hard, high-dimensional control tasks.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: task renders, then two learning-curve plots
description: A three-part horizontal figure. Panel (a), on the left, is a two-row strip of simulator renderings of black humanoid robots. The top row shows a robot shooting a basketball at a hoop across four frames. The bottom row shows a robot holding a balancing pose on a platform. Panels (b) and (c) are line plots titled Basketball and Balance Hard, with environment steps on the x-axis and episode return on the y-axis. Each plot has a legend for DreamerV3, PPO, SAC, TD-MPC2, FastTD3 and FastDSAC. The FastDSAC curve is blue with a wide light-blue min-max band. The FastTD3 curve is black with a gray band. The other baselines stay flat near zero. The blue curve climbs well above the black one, and the eye goes to that gap. The captions below are in a large serif font.
caption: Performance of FastDSAC on very high-dimensional humanoid control tasks. (a) Visualizations of the challenging Basketball and Balance Hard environments. (b, c) Evaluation curves comparing FastDSAC with the FastTD3 baseline. Curves show the mean over 5 seeds, with shaded regions spanning the min-max range across seeds. FastDSAC outperforms FastTD3, achieving final returns 1.8× and 3.5× higher on the respective tasks with stronger sample efficiency.
abstract: Scaling Maximum Entropy Reinforcement Learning (RL) to high-dimensional humanoid control remains a fundamental challenge, as the ''curse of dimensionality'' induces severe exploration inefficiency and training instability. Consequently, highly optimized deterministic policy gradients currently dominate high-throughput regimes. We address this limitation with FastDSAC, a framework that effectively unlocks the potential of maximum entropy stochastic policies for complex continuous control. We introduce Dimension-wise Entropy Modulation (DEM) to dynamically redistribute the exploration budget, alongside a continuous distributional critic tailored to ensure accurate value estimation by mitigating both high-dimensional overestimation and discrete quantization artifacts. Extensive evaluations on HumanoidBench and a diverse set of continuous control tasks demonstrate that FastDSAC establishes state-of-the-art performance for high-dimensional stochastic policies on the evaluated benchmarks. Our method is competitive with and often outperforms strong deterministic baselines, with gains of 180% and 350% on the challenging Basketball and Balance Hard tasks, respectively.
